request.objective:
You are the lead of swarm tight-271 in Baton, the cross-agent coordination harness this repository is. This swarm has two purposes at once: deliver issue #271 (read it: gh issue view 271), and exercise Baton's DECLARED tight coupling on real work while the root orchestrator audits it from outside. Use the coupling verbs the runtime now has (docs/39-swarm-runtime.md, the 2026-09-13 coupling section; docs/audits/2026-09-13-runtime-policy/coupling.md; impl/test/swarm-coupling.test.mjs shows every payload): work_updated.dependsOn, swarm.coupling_updated (synchronization points: declare/arrive/release; exclusive writer over a shared checkout), group failure policy.

Plan the work as two units with a real dependency, in ONE shared checkout:
- W1 "projections" — in impl/src/swarm-state.mjs and impl/src/swarm-runtime.mjs: (a) each participant row on swarm.view carries `guidance`: the guides addressed to it, projected from the existing message.sent rows (kind nudge, to.workerId = the participant's worker) as [{seq, ts, from, messageId}] — no new events; (b) `swarm.guide` returns the row it wrote (seq, ts, messageId) instead of only ok; (c) each participant row carries `workspace: {physicalOwnerId, shared, holderCount}` from the custody rows capture already reads; (d) every projected row (work, assignments, context, contributions, reviews, couplings) carries its `seq` and `ts` where it does not already.
- W2 "refusals and surface" — depends on W1's accepted contribution: (a) a refused swarm mutation (swarm_command_invalid, swarm_permission_required, version_conflict, swarm_holder_live, and the coupling refusals) is recorded as a durable `swarm.operation_refused` row {command, event, code, field, participantId} that wakes a watch (add it to impl/src/swarm-event-schemas.mjs and swarm-contract.mjs like the other kinds; replay byte-identical); (b) the swarm surface (impl/src/swarm-surface.mjs, CLI.md, MCP.md via `node impl/scripts/surface-gate.mjs --write`) documents guidance, workspace and refusal rows with examples; (c) tests for both in impl/test/swarm-*.test.mjs, copying the fixture style of swarm-coupling.test.mjs.

Recruit two workers (you hold recruit): "projections" for W1 with options {"exact":{"harness":"omp","model":"zai/glm-5.3-flash","effort":"max"}} and "surface" for W2 with options {"exact":{"harness":"omp","model":"deepseek/deepseek-flash","effort":"max"},"shareWorkspaceWith":"projections"} so both work in ONE checkout. Declare W2's dependency on W1 (dependsOn), declare a synchronization point "gate" both arrive at before anyone runs `node impl/scripts/surface-gate.mjs --write`, and declare the exclusive writer over the shared checkout so only one of them edits at a time (release it when handing over). Assign, guide, watch, and review through the swarm only. When W1 is accepted, W2 proceeds; if a worker chooses to proceed against an unsettled dependency, that is allowed but must be visible — say so in your report.

When both contributions are accepted: write docs/audits/2026-09-14-tight-coupling/lead.md — for each coupling record (dependency, synchronization point, exclusive writer, failure policy) what you declared, what each worker saw in its view (quote them), what woke your watch, every refusal verbatim, the time it took, gaps, frictions and insights; then publish swarm.contribution_recorded naming the file and end your turn so the root captures. Constraints: verification is `node impl/scripts/run-suite.mjs` and must be GREEN for the code contributions (the workers run it themselves before publishing; do not run swarm.check on your own docs); no numeric defaults that act as limits; a budget threshold notification is evidence, not a stop; never print environment variables containing tokens.
